en: Now, the Hymn to the Nine Planets.
The Sun.
I bow down to the Sun, who resembles a hibiscus flower, the son of Kaśyapa, possessed of great splendor, the enemy of darkness, and the destroyer of all sins. 1.
Soma.
I bow to the Moon, the Soma, who resembles curd, a conch shell, and snow; who is born from the Ocean of Milk; and who is the ornament upon the crown of Śambhu. 2.
Auspiciousness.
I bow down to that auspicious youth, born from the womb of the earth, possessing a radiance equal to the luster of lightning, and holding a spear in his hand. 3.
Budha (Mercury)
I bow down to that Budha, who is dark as a priyaṅgu bud, peerless in form, gentle, and endowed with gentle qualities. 4.
The Guru.
I bow to that Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of the gods and the sages, who resembles gold, who is the embodiment of intelligence, and the lord of the three worlds. ||5||
Śukra.
I bow down to Bhārgava, who resembles the lotus stalk of the snowy mountains, the supreme preceptor of the Daityas, and the expounder of all scriptures.
Saturn.
I bow to Śanaiścara, who has the luster of blue collyrium, the son of Ravi, the elder brother of Yama, born from Chāyā and Ārtaṇḍa.
Rāhu.
I bow down to that Rāhu, who possesses a body of half-measure, who is endowed with great prowess, who eclipses the sun and the moon, and who was born from the womb of Siṃhikā. ||8||
The Banner-Bearer (Ketu).
I bow down to that Ketu, which resembles a palāśa flower, whose head is adorned with stars and planets, and who is fierce, of a fierce nature, and terrible. 9.
The Declaration of the Fruit.
Whoever, being well-composed, recites this which has been sung from the mouth of Vyāsa,
whether by day or by night, there shall be the pacification of obstacles.
For men, women, and kings, it shall be the destroyer of evil dreams;
it bestows incomparable sovereignty and increases health and nourishment for them.
The afflictions arising from planets and constellations, as well as those produced by thieves and fire—all these are pacified; Vyāsa declares this without a doubt.
Thus ends the hymn to the nine planets, beginning with Āditya, composed by the venerable Vyāsa.
Now follows the hymn for removing the affliction caused by the nine planets.
The Sun.
The Sun is the first of the planets and the protector of the world;
may Ravi remove from me the suffering born of unfavorable planetary positions. (1)
Soma.
May the Moon—the lord of Rohiṇī, whose form is nectar, whose body is nectar, and who feeds on nectar—remove my suffering born from an adverse planetary position. 2.
Auspiciousness.
May Mars, the son of the Earth, possessed of great splendor, who is ever the cause of fear for the worlds, both the sender of rain and the withdrawer of rain, remove my affliction. 3.
Budha (Mercury)
May Budha, the son of Candra, who is of great splendor, the cause of portents for the worlds, the learned one who brings joy to the Sun, remove my affliction. 4.
The Guru.
May my preceptor—the minister of the gods, Viśālākṣa, who is ever devoted to the welfare of the world and surrounded by many disciples—remove my suffering. (5)
Śukra.
May Bhrigu—the minister of the Daityas, the preceptor of them all, the giver of their life, and the lord of the planets Tārā and Graha—remove my affliction. (6)
Saturn.
May Śani, the son of the Sun, who has a tall body, wide eyes, and is dear to Śiva;
who possesses long-standing conduct and a serene soul—may he remove my suffering. (7)
Rāhu.
May he who possesses hundreds and thousands of eyes, appearing in manifold forms and colors as a portent for the worlds, remove my darkness of suffering. 8.
The Banner-Bearer (Ketu).
May Śikhī—possessing a great head, a great mouth, long fangs, and great strength, with a massive body and hair standing erect—remove my suffering. 9.
Thus ends the hymn for removing the afflictions of the nine planets as declared in the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa.
